text:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV2: High error rate for websocket streams from Globex on dedicated pool vpc-dedicated-77. Spike in 504/connection timeouts starting 11:03 UTC. Paging maya (oncall).

maya: Oncall ack. @globex-sre can you confirm if you rolled anything in your gateway or did any cert/ssl rotation?

globex-sre: We did a config push at 10:45 to switch LB health-check policy and enable aggressive client-side reconnect (internal lib) until we finish a rollout. No cert changes.

jordan: Telemetry: aggregated `ws_disconnect` events for tenant globex are up 3x. Regular REST token generation still fine. Streaming sessions show many `websocket close (1006)` and `frame read timeout`.

liam: Checking infra: dedicated pool proxies show increasing `accept` backlog and worker threads spiking. Kernel shows SYN flood-like markers but mostly coming from a set of Globex IP ranges (their app servers).

sam-support: Customer impact: Globex realtime annotations failing intermittently, users see "connection lost" and manual refresh required. They've flagged 500 customers impacted. They're asking for timeline and whether we can throttle their traffic server-side.

incident-bot: Suspected scope: tenant-scoped. Engagement policy: SEV2.

maya: Hypothesis: their client reconnect pattern combined with our proxy worker limit causes threads to pile up; when worker pool exhausted proxies return 504 or drop. Immediate mitigations: A) ask Globex to throttle reconnects (increase backoff + jitter) — might be slow; B) apply per-tenant egress throttle + connection cap on dedicated proxies; C) temporarily route Globex streaming to a staging dedicated pool (vpc-dedicated-88) that has higher worker capacity; D) convert streaming to chunked HTTP fallback for existing sessions. Which can we do fastest?

jordan: We can add a per-tenant limit via `redwoodctl quota set --tenant globex --max-stream-conns 200` in ~2m; that will soft-queue excess new streams. Routing swap to vpc-dedicated-88 requires infra approval and ~15m. HTTP chunked fallback is non-trivial for client compatibility.

liam: I can deploy a temporary iptables rule on the proxy fleet to rate-limit new connections from their IP ranges (tc + connlimit) in ~6m. That will blunt the reconnect surge without touching their app. Risk: might affect legitimate bursts.

globex-sre: We can push a client patch to add jitter but won't be immediate for prod. We'll accept a temporary server-side throttle.

maya: Okay, plan: 1) liam apply soft connlimit for Globex IPs, 2) jordan set tenant max-stream-conns to 200, 3) if errors remain after 10m, perform routing to vpc-dedicated-88. Sam will keep customer updated.

liam: Preparing firewall rule: 
```
# limit new TCP connections per src IP for globex ranges
tc qdisc add dev eth0 handle 1: htb default 12
iptables -A INPUT -s 203.0.113.0/24 -m connlimit --connlimit-above 8 -j DROP
```
Applying in 4m to a canary host first.

jordan: Executing `redwoodctl quota set --tenant globex --max-stream-conns 200 --scope dedicated` now.

incident-bot: Action logged: tenant quota modified at 11:12 UTC.

liam: Canary firewall applied. Observing reduced burst acceptance on canary but downstream service healthy. Rolling to remaining proxy hosts in 6m window with gradual ramp.

maya: Monitoring metrics. @sam-support please let Globex know we applied a short-term server-side throttle to stabilize sessions; sharing timeline.

sam-support: Notified Globex support lead. They acknowledged and asked for ETA to full resolution.

maya: Telemetry update @11:25 UTC: ws_disconnects dropping from 3x -> 1.6x baseline. User complaints down. Good sign. Keeping throttle in place while we plan more permanent fix.

globex-sre: Seeing improvements. We will coordinate a client-side backoff roll tomorrow. Thanks.

eng-runtime: Notes from runtime: our websocket accept loop does not have per-tenant backpressure awareness; reconnect storms can starve thread pool. We should add a tenant-level accept gate and token-bucket to smooth bursts.

jordan: Proposed post-incident actions: 1) tenant accept gate + token-bucket on dedicated proxies; 2) add `redwoodctl route swap --tenant <t> --fallback-pool` safe primitive; 3) onboarding checklist for enterprise: recommended LB healthcheck and reconnect limits.

liam: Also proposing: add a canary test harness that simulates bad-client reconnect patterns so we can tune default connlimit and worker pool sizes.

maya: Handoff: I'm going offline at 12:00 UTC. Jordan will own watch. Jordan, please create RCA ticket and schedule hotfix for runtime within next sprint if possible.

jordan: Taking over. Will keep 30m watch and raise priority tickets: SRE-501 (proxy token-bucket) and ENG-RUNTIME-210 (accept gate). I'll also coordinate with Globex for joint testing.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated at 11:38 UTC (throttles and quota applied). Status: mitigated. Paging closed.

sam-support: Customer updated: they're comfortable with mitigation and want a postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix.

maya: Closing notes: Mitigation that worked: per-tenant connlimit + quota. Root cause likely aggressive client reconnect coupled with missing per-tenant backpressure on the accept path. Long term: runtime changes + enterprise onboarding doc + a safe routing primitive.

jordan: +15m check-in: metrics stable. Scheduling postmortem meeting and will attach timeline and exported logs.

incident-bot: Thread archived at 12:01 UTC.
